The tested form is of positive type: $W(g,g)\ge0$ for every $g$.

Its vacuum covariance is the positive-type distribution $$C_\kappa(s)=-\frac{\kappa^2}{16\pi}\,\operatorname{csch}^2\!\left(\frac{\kappa}{2}(s-i0)\right).$$ Here the notation is fixed as follows: for $b=\kappa/2$, set $Y_b(s)=\sinh(bs)/b$. Since $Y_b'(s)=\cosh(bs)>0$ and $Y_b(s)\to\pm\infty$ as $s\to\pm\infty$, it is a smooth increasing diffeomorphism. Define $\operatorname{csch}^2(b(s-i0)):=b^{-2}Y_b^*((y-i0)^{-2})$, where $$\langle Y_b^*T,\varphi\rangle:=\left\langle T,\varphi(Y_b^{-1}(y))(Y_b^{-1})'(y)\right\rangle.$$

The bosonic operators on their displayed domains are closed and mutually adjoint, and on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ satisfy $$[a(h),a^\dagger(k)]=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad [a(h),a(k)]=[a^\dagger(h),a^\dagger(k)]=0.$$
Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$, with $a<b$. Then there is $c\in(a,b)$ such that $$ f(b)-f(a)=f'(c)(b-a). $$
